3 PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 15.11.2018 passed in MVC No.879/2017 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Harihara, (for short 'the Tribunal'),
respondent Nos.2, 3 and 4 therein have preferred MFA.No.2290/2019 and petitioners therein have preferred MFA.No.1622/2020.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Harihara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 02.08.2017 at about 4.30 p.m. the deceased Sudeep was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-17-F-1294, while proceeding near Alaganchekere village road, the driver applied the break suddenly, due to which the deceased who was sitting on the seat near to the back door, lost control and fell down on the door, due to which the door opened and consequently fell outside the bus.
As a result, the deceased Sudeep sustained grievous injuries and died.
Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are his parents.
Petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased.
Hence, they preferred MVC No. 879/2017 before the Tribunal.

4. Based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, the Tribunal concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent riding of the KSRTC bus and awarded compensation of Rs.15,74,440/- to the petitioners along with interest @ 6% per annum.

Aggrieved by the same,
respondent Nos.2, 3 and 4 have preferred MFA.No.2290/2019 and the petitioners have preferred MFA.NO.1622/2020.
5. The case of the petitioners is that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

The case of respondent Nos.2, 3 and 4 is that the accident happened due to negligence on part of the deceased and not the driver of the bus and even otherwise, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
6.
PW.1 nor RW.1 are eye witnesses to the incident.
Though RW.1 was driving the bus, he has not seen the accident happening.

Under the circumstances, the Tribunal has relied upon the charge sheet filed by the Police after due investigation against the driver of the bus and based on the available material has concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the bus.
The KSRTC is not in a position to show as to why the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal has to be discarded.
Under the circumstances, I see no reason to interfere with the conclusion arrived by the Tribunal that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the bus.
Having concluded thus, the only question that arises for consideration is whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just, fair and reasonable.
7. Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2017.
The income of the deceased is not established before the Tribunal.
As per the chart prepared by the Lok-Adalat, the notional income to be taken for the year 2017 is Rs.11,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 18 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '18' has to be adopted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As The Divisional Controller vs Smt Chandrakala on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78409436/
4 per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% needs to be added to his income.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As he was a bachelor, 50% of his income is deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,63,200/- (11,000 + 40% x 12 x 18 x 1/2).

8. Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are three dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium (Rs.40,000x3= 1,20,000).

sentences.text: Further, petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,13,200/- as against Rs.15,74,440/- awarded by the Tribunal.
vii) Draw modified award accordingly;
